newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cosmo says it will hold off buying Iraqi crude.
newsitem.headline: Cosmo says it will hold off buying Iraqi crude.

text.p: Cosmo Oil Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it will not buy Iraqi crude oil for the time being, although it may do so in the future.
"We will not be buying crude oil for the time being," a company spokesman said.
Asked about possible future purchases, the spokesman said the company would consider the step "positively".

Mitsubishi Corp is believed to be the only Japanese company to have signed an agreement to buy Iraqi crude under the U.N. oil-for-food deal which allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil, its first oil sales since sanctions were imposed after Baghdad's invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
The Japanese trading company is acting on behalf of five Japanese oil companies, which together will lift 40,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) from Iraq under a three-month agreement.
Cosmo was not one of the five.
Japan was importing roughly 200,000 bpd of crude oil from Iraq before the United Nations imposed sanctions against Iraq.
